subject.title: Telegram: Auto-reply to unauthorized group senders with admin contact instructions

question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in Telegram reply for non-allowlisted group senders, and what rate-limit, admin-contact, raw-ID, topic, and default-silent semantics should it use?
rationale: The request changes behavior at a Telegram authorization-denial boundary and may expose raw user IDs or amplify group messages, so cleanup automation cannot safely choose the permanent product/security contract.

options.title: Add Opt-In Rate-Limited Notice
options.body: Add a Telegram plugin setting for a denied-sender onboarding notice with per-chat/topic/sender cooldown, configurable admin-contact wording, and documented raw-ID handling.

options.title: Route Through Operator Audit
options.body: Keep unauthorized senders silent and satisfy visibility through owner notification or denied-inbound audit work such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/77546.

options.title: Keep Silent Denial
options.body: Decline sender-facing replies for now and document `groupAllowFrom`, logs, and manual ID discovery as the supported secure posture.

recommendation.title: Add Opt-In Rate-Limited Notice
recommendation.body: Add a Telegram plugin setting for a denied-sender onboarding notice with per-chat/topic/sender cooldown, configurable admin-contact wording, and documented raw-ID handling.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current blame and adjacent docs/config/channel history for this Telegram authorization surface.
